title: 题李凝幽居
titleEn: Written at Li Ning’s Hidden Home
author: 贾岛
intro: A poet visits a friend who lives far from the world, finds him out, and leaves a promise to come back. This is the poem behind the Chinese word 推敲 (“push or knock”), which still means weighing every word.
analysis: 贾岛去拜访隐居的朋友李凝，没有见到人，就在门上题了这首诗。开头写住处的冷清：很少有邻居，长满草的小路通向荒废的园子。第三、四句最有名：鸟已经在池边的树上睡了，一个和尚在月光下敲门。传说贾岛骑在驴上，想不好用“推”还是“敲”，一边想一边做手势，撞上了大官韩愈的车队。韩愈不但没生气，还替他想了想，说“敲”字好——夜深人静，敲门声更显出四周的安静。从此“推敲”成了一个词，意思是反复斟酌字句。后四句写回去路上的山野景色，最后说：我暂时走了，还会再来，不会忘记约定。
analysisEn: Jia Dao went to visit his friend Li Ning, who lived as a recluse, but no one seemed to be home, so he wrote this poem — traditionally on the door itself. The first lines set the scene: hardly any neighbours, a grassy path leading into an overgrown garden. Then comes the famous couplet: birds asleep in the trees by the pond, and a monk knocking at a gate under the moon. The story goes that Jia Dao, riding a donkey, couldn’t decide between “push” (推) and “knock” (敲). Lost in thought and miming both gestures, he rode straight into the procession of the senior official Han Yu. Instead of punishing him, Han Yu thought it over and chose “knock”: on a silent night, a knock makes the stillness even deeper. Ever since, 推敲 has been an everyday Chinese word for carefully weighing your words. The second half follows the walk home — a bridge dividing the colours of the fields, stones that seem to move the roots of the clouds — and ends with a promise: I’m leaving for now, but I’ll be back, and I won’t break our appointment.
background: Jia Dao (779–843) was a monk before he returned to lay life and tried, mostly without success, to build an official career. He was famous for polishing single lines for years; this poem and its “push or knock” story are the best-known example.
pronunciation: 多音字：少邻并 shǎo（少，不多）；邻并 bìng（并，靠在一起）；还来此 huán（回来）；分野色 fēn。
version: 采用通行版本（《全唐诗》）。“推敲”的故事见宋代笔记，属传说，解析里照传说讲。

lines.lit: A quiet dwelling, few neighbours beside it;
lines.en: He lives at ease, with hardly a neighbour near;

lines.lit: a grassy path enters an overgrown garden.
lines.en: a grassy path runs into a wild garden.

lines.lit: Birds roost in the trees by the pond;
lines.en: Birds have settled in the trees by the pond,

lines.lit: a monk knocks at a gate beneath the moon.
lines.en: and a monk knocks at a gate in the moonlight.

lines.lit: Crossing the bridge, the colours of the fields divide;
lines.en: Over the bridge, the fields split into two colours;

lines.lit: moving past stones, the roots of the clouds stir.
lines.en: the stones I pass seem to shift the roots of clouds.

lines.lit: I leave for a while, but will come back here;
lines.en: I go for now, but I will come again —

lines.lit: our quiet appointment — I will not break my word.
lines.en: our quiet promise is one I’ll keep.

words.note: 古义：隐居的住处。现代汉语偶尔用于书面语。

words.en: to live at leisure, away from office

words.note: 古代说法，现代汉语说“邻居”。
“径”就是小路，现代汉语还有“小径”“捷径”。

words.en: to stay for the night; (of birds) to roost

words.note: 现代汉语说“和尚”；“僧人”是书面语。
来自这首诗的故事，今天是常用词：“这句话还要再推敲推敲。”

words.en: the colours of the open country
“cloud roots” — rocks (clouds were thought to rise from stones)
words.note: 古人认为云从山石中生出，所以把石头叫“云根”。现代汉语不用。

words.en: a quiet appointment (to meet again in seclusion)
to fail to keep; to let down
words.note: 现代汉语还有“辜负”“负约”。

imagery.name: 鸟
imagery.zh: 鸟已归巢入睡，说明夜已深，衬托出幽居的安静。
imagery.en: The birds have gone to roost: it is late, and the hidden home is utterly still.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 月光下敲门，画面清冷安静，是全诗最有名的一句。
imagery.en: A knock under the moon — a cool, quiet picture, and the most famous line of the poem.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: “云根”指山石，写回去路上的山野，也写出隐居处远离尘世。
imagery.en: “Cloud roots” are the rocks on the hillside — a reminder of how far from the world the friend lives.

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: 长满草的小路说明来的人很少，主人过着隐居生活。
imagery.en: The overgrown path shows that few visitors ever come: the owner lives in seclusion.
